name: getColFilters() ignores a column's own switches
why: Every input is matched with the OWNER's flags again, as before sa_enable_column_filter_modes. The Release chip's Ex then changes nothing: 'live' stays at 4 rows instead of 52. Must fail.
grep: a column's Ex inverts that column

name: _colFilterFlags() always answers with the owner's flags
why: The status line and the 📊 banner read a column's flags through _colFilterFlags(). Answering with the owner's boxes drops the column's own (ex) from the status text and the banner from the panel. Must fail on the 📊 test (banner count 1 expected).

name: a chip click does not re-run the filter
why: The chip toggles its state but no pass runs, so the table keeps showing the pre-toggle rows until the next keystroke — the F3 defect again, one level down. Must fail.
grep: a column's Ex inverts that column

name: the sub-table boxes re-run column filters although they no longer govern them
why: Drops the !_colFilterModesOn() guard in applySubTableModes(), so ticking a sub-table box with a column filter typed runs a full runFilter() pass again. The result is the same — getColFilters() ignores the owner's flags per input — so only the wasted pass changes. KNOWN OVERLAP, recorded: no spec can see it.

name: the column ✕ keeps the switches
why: Removes the reset from the ✕ handler. The Ex chip stays pressed and the next text typed is inverted. Must fail.

name: a chip mousedown takes focus from the field
why: Without the capture-phase preventDefault the button takes focus on mousedown and the next keystroke goes nowhere. Must fail on the caret test.
grep: leaves the caret in the filter field

name: the container query never switches to the compact button
why: A 0 px query never matches, so every cell shows chips whatever its width. Must fail: the page's narrow columns must show the button.

name: the default threshold goes back to 130 px
why: The value first proposed. Between ~130 and ~155 px the chips cover the middle of the field, which the default-threshold test asserts cannot happen (elementFromPoint at the field's centre must be the field) and which also breaks its 'button iff width <= 160'. Must fail.

name: the filter cell is never made a query container
why: Without .mb-col-modes the wrapper is no container, the @container rule has nothing to measure, and the compact button never shows even when forced (threshold 5000). Must fail.
grep: the button opens the switches in a pop-up

name: Ctrl+Click on a global box sets nothing on the columns
why: Removes the bulk-set from the global boxes' click listener. The Rx box ticks, the columns' Rx chips stay off. Must fail.
grep: Click on a global box also sets

name: Ctrl+Click on a sub-table box sets nothing on its columns
why: Removes the bulk-set from the sub-table boxes' click listener. Must fail: sub-table 0's Ex chips must all be pressed.
grep: Click on a sub-table box sets

name: Ctrl+Click on a sub-table box reaches the other sub-tables too
why: Bulk-sets every column of the PAGE instead of this sub-table's. Must fail: sub-table 1 must stay untouched.
grep: Click on a sub-table box sets

name: the 📊 panel never shows the Ex banner
why: Removes the banner. Must fail on the 📊 test (banner count 1 expected with the column's Ex on).

name: 'Apply these modes to every column' applies to one column
why: Copies the modes only onto the pop-up's own target. Must fail: every button in the table must read C·R.
grep: Apply these modes to every column

name: the setting cannot be switched off
why: _colFilterModesOn() always answers true. With the setting off the chips still appear and the global Ex no longer inverts the column filter. Must fail.

name: a stale filter-row rebuild drops the switches
why: addColumnFilterRow()'s rebuild restores values but no longer the data-mb-mode-* attributes. KNOWN UNCOVERED: the rebuild only runs when a column is added AFTER the first build (the Picard column, a second cleanupHeaders pass), which no fixture can trigger after a user has set a switch. Recorded rather than left unmentioned.
grep: a column's switch survives the re-render
